title: Why, and how you need to sandbox AI-Generated Code? — Harshil Agrawal, Cloudflare
talk_summary: Harshil Agrawal (Cloudflare) argues AI-generated code is functionally untrusted code from the internet and should be sandboxed with capability-based security: default-deny, explicit minimal grants. He contrasts V8 isolates (fast, no filesystem/processes, for tool calls and code interpreters) with containers (real Linux, for builds/dev servers), and gives an 8-point checklist: deny network, explicit capabilities, per-user isolation, resource limits, secrets outside the sandbox, cleanup with try/finally, logging, input validation.

takeaways.technique: Match sandbox strength to task: isolates for tool calls, containers for builds
takeaways.what_they_do: Uses V8 isolates for fast, constrained execution of generated functions/tool calls (sub-ms, no filesystem, no processes) and full Linux containers only when the task needs git clone, npm install, or a dev server.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Does the code need a file system, processes, or package installs? If yes, it's container. Full stop. If no, isolates.
takeaways.numbers: isolates start in ~0.25 ms; containers take seconds; Cloudflare container default timeout 10 min

takeaways.what_they_do: Sets globalOutbound to null so generated code cannot make any outbound request unless explicitly routed through a controlled proxy with allowlisted domains and logging.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This single line blocks all outbound network request. No fetch, no web socket, no HTTP. Nothing gets out.

takeaways.technique: Secrets never enter the sandbox; proxy through the orchestrator
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of passing API keys as env vars into the sandbox, the sandbox calls a worker proxy endpoint that injects the real auth header and forwards the request.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The moment the API key enters the sandbox, any code running inside the container can read it

takeaways.technique: Per-run isolation boundary + guaranteed teardown with max lifetime
takeaways.what_they_do: One user/run per sandbox, never shared; destroy in try/finally even on failure, and set maximum lifetimes so idle sandboxes die.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Always use try finally, not try catch. Try finally. Even if the build fails

takeaways.technique: Resource limits to stop runaway generated code
takeaways.what_they_do: Caps CPU time and memory per sandbox so a hallucinated infinite loop or unbounded allocation cannot burn the compute budget or take down the host.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Don't let a hallucinating LLM infinite loop burn through your compute budget or take down your servers.

takeaways.technique: Validate generated code before execution + log every run
takeaways.what_they_do: Applies basic pre-execution checks (length limits, syntax validation, known dangerous pattern detection) as defense in depth, and logs what code ran, when, who triggered it, and what it did.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Validate the input before it hits the sandbox. Basic checks on the code before you execute it.
